They finally got Boggan's word to let them off if they could get the old Justice of the peace to let them off, which they succeeded in doing, but not without tears and the promising never to do it again; so it all quieted down. I suppose this was the biggest noise-making one there.

I recall on one Friday afternoon that Barlow and Palo Roberts, brother Robert, and myself organized a fishing and camping trip to Red River. The round trip was about forty-five miles. We went in one boat, and fish a-'plenty'—(my first view of Red River). Early and faithful Friday we came back our way in a wagon with a sack of flour meal to fry fish and eat on the way home, so we did.

Social Life and Entertainment

Mr. Galbraith, Fort Worth, Texas, July 13, 1938.¹
